title: Introduce unit-econ template importer and quant sanity checker
author: Priya Ramesh
description:
Motivation: We frequently see tenants override defaults in a way that regresses unit economics (higher per-token cost or latency spikes) after model/quant rollouts. This PR introduces a small, auditable path to import 'unit-econ templates' as code and a lightweight quant sanity checker that runs as part of CI and as an on-demand validation step in the Console. The goal is to reduce manual error when applying tenant defaults and to catch quantization-induced quality drift before rollouts.

What this PR adds (high level):
- CLI importer: `redwood unit-econ import <yaml>` which merges template YAML into the tenant-defaults store with validation and dry-run support.
- Template schema: a validated YAML schema (examples under cfg/defaults/unit_econ_templates.yaml) for batching, cache hints, and quant modality suggestions.
- Quant sanity checker: a small Go service (server/quant/sanity_checker.go) that executes a bounded simulation (synthetic micro-inference) comparing FP32 baseline outputs to candidate quantized model outputs using configurable tolerances; reports a quality score and known-failure fingerprints. The checker is plumbed into CI and can be invoked by product rules during a tenant rollout.
- Docs: developer guide for the importer and the sanity checker (docs/unit-econ-importer.md) with examples and recommended thresholds.
- Tests: unit tests for importer validation and an integration smoke harness that exercises the quant checker in a mocked runtime.

Files of note (high level):
- cli/unit_econ/importer.py: CLI entrypoint, validations, and dry-run code path.
- cfg/defaults/unit_econ_templates.yaml: curated seed templates for sandbox and production tiers.
- server/quant/sanity_checker.go: quant comparison runner and summary exporter.
- docs/unit-econ-importer.md: usage and rollout recommendations.
- tests/unit/test_importer.py, tests/integration/test_quant_sanity.py: coverage for core flows.

Checklist: 
- [x] Schema and validator for templates
- [x] CLI import/dry-run path
- [x] Quant sanity checker with pluggable thresholds
- [x] CI integration (see pipeline changes)
- [x] Developer docs and sample templates
- [x] Unit + integration tests

Testing notes and CI: The first CI run surfaced a flaky assertion in the mocked inference harness (tests/integration/test_quant_sanity.py). I tightened the timeout and added a retry around the harness startup; second pipeline run passed. CI checks included: lint, unit-tests (py/go), integration-smoke, telemetry-schema-check. Artifacts contain the sanity_checker report (json) on success.

Migration and rollout plan: The importer is additive and requires opt-in via Console or CLI. Seed templates are non-authoritative—importing writes a tenant-level template draft which must be applied by an operator. The sanity checker is enabled in 'preflight' mode for early rollouts and will block a rollout only if the configured quality score drops below the tenant's safety threshold. We will monitor Console telemetry for template adoption and any denied rollouts for 2 weeks post-merge.

Related: This complements ENG-1734 (unit-econ audits) and ENG-1901 (tenant defaults UI work).

review_comments: Ethan Park: Can we add telemetry metrics for template import failures and sanity-check scores? We should be able to answer 'how many imports failed validation' and 'distribution of quality scores' before enabling blocking mode.
Priya Ramesh: Added metrics (metrics.import.validation_failures, metrics.quant.sanity_score) and exported them to the telemetry bridge. See server/quant/sanity_checker.go lines ~120 for the exporter.

Maya Lind: The quant checker is great — please make thresholds configurable per-tenant and not hard-coded in cfg. Also add a clear fallback that does NOT block rollouts for tenants with 'non-blocking' mode.

Priya Ramesh: Thresholds are pluggable via tenant defaults now; importer schema includes 'safety.mode = {blocking | advisory}' and 'safety.threshold'. Default is 'advisory' until we flip the Console toggle.
Daniel Ortiz: Tests look good — one nit: reduce the seed template verbosity to avoid leaking internal notes into public docs. Also add a short README in cfg/defaults explaining purpose.
Priya Ramesh: Removed internal notes and added cfg/defaults/README.md explaining template usage and intended audience.
release_notes: Add 'unit-econ template importer' CLI and a quant sanity checker to detect quant-induced quality regressions before rollouts. Includes seed templates and docs. (opt-in, advisory by default)
